test_title: PYST 55: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true for Read-Only Memory (ROM)?

options.text: It stores the booting instructions permanently.
It is volatile memory that stores data temporarily.
It stores data that can be modified by the user.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It stores the booting instructions permanently.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Read-Only Memory (ROM)** is a type of non-volatile memory, meaning it retains its data even when the power is turned off.
 
• It stores the **booting instructions permanently**, such as the Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) or firmware required to start a computer or device.
 
• The data stored in ROM is **pre-programmed** during the manufacturing process and cannot be modified or erased by the user under normal conditions.
 
• ROM is essential for hardware initialization and provides the instructions required for the operating system to load into Random Access Memory (RAM).
 
• It is widely used in various devices, including computers, smartphones, and embedded systems, for storing critical instructions and firmware.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Read-Only Memory (ROM)**

 
 
• ROM is essential for storing firmware, which acts as the interface between hardware and software.
 
• Types of ROM include Mask ROM, PROM (Programmable ROM), EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM), and EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM).
 
• In modern devices, Flash Memory, a type of EEPROM, is commonly used for storing firmware and other data.
